app.name: Browser Switch
cli.usage.title: Browser Switch - Smart URL Interceptor & Browser Switcher
cli.usage.desc:
When set as default browser, URLs are intercepted: matching domain rules open directly,
otherwise a picker lets you choose a browser.

Options:
cli.flag.test: Test URL matching (print result and exit)
cli.flag.list_profiles: List detected browser profiles and exit
cli.flag.check_default: Check if this is the default browser
cli.output.no_profiles: No multi-profile configurations detected (or only single default)
cli.output.is_default: ✅ BrowserSwitch is currently the default browser
cli.output.install_success: ✅ Installation successful! BrowserSwitch has been set as default browser
cli.output.install_manual: ⚠️  macOS requires manual confirmation: System Settings has been opened, please select BrowserSwitch in 'Default Web Browser'.
cli.output.rule_fallback: Rule browser failed to open, falling back to picker
picker.title: Choose a browser to open
picker.countdown: Auto-open in %d seconds with %s · any action cancels
settings.browsers.favorites_hint: Determines popup display order and ⌘ number

settings.add_rule.title: Add Rule
settings.edit_rule.title: Edit Rule
settings.add_rule.hint.new_window: When checked, matches always open a new window instead of reusing an existing one
settings.add_rule.modehint.exact: Matches only when the URL's domain is exactly what you typed. E.g. example.com will not match www.example.com.
settings.add_rule.modehint.urlequal: Matches only when the whole URL (scheme, path and query string included) is exactly what you typed. Most specific.
settings.add_rule.modehint.contains: Matches whenever your text appears anywhere in the domain or the full URL. Most permissive.
settings.add_rule.modehint.prefix: Matches when the domain or the full URL starts with your text. E.g. https:// matches every secure link.
settings.add_rule.modehint.suffix: Matches when the domain or the full URL ends with your text. E.g. .pdf matches every PDF link.
settings.add_rule.modehint.wildcard: Use * for any run of characters and ? for a single one. Use this when you need finer control.
settings.add_rule.modehint.regex: Match the domain or the full URL with a regular expression. Most powerful, requires some background.
settings.add_rule.hint.pattern: Supports full domain, wildcards (* and ?), regular expressions
settings.add_rule.hint.mode: Auto-suggested after input, or select manually
settings.add_rule.hint.browser: URLs matching this rule will open in this browser
settings.add_rule.error.invalid_priority: Priority must be a non-negative integer
settings.add_rule.error.urlequal_need_sc: "Full URL equal" needs a complete URL starting with http:// or https://, e.g. https://example.com/a/b
settings.add_rule.error.exact_has_scheme: "Domain equal" takes a bare domain like example.com, without http://. Use "Full URL equal" to match a whole URL.
settings.add_rule.error.exact_has_path: "Domain equal" cannot contain a path. Use "Contains" or "Wildcard" to match paths.
settings.add_rule.error.quick_has_glob: "Contains/Prefix/Suffix" treat * and ? as literal characters, not wildcards. Remove them or switch to the "Wildcard" mode.
settings.add_rule.error.duplicate: An identical rule (%s) already targets the same browser; no need to add it twice
